item: The all-history top-terms query sums per keyword id before the text grouping, so it answers where the one-step grouping ran out of memory
summary: At the 1,004 MB tier the all-history most-mentioned query (the text the serve and the serve canary both run) failed with the engine's memory error at 20, 24 and 28 M mentions on generated corpora (one run per size) and the serve answered an empty list (counted as a top-terms fallback; R194 later made it go live). It now sums keyword_daily per keyword_id in an inner query, joins keyword_meta to that and keeps the text grouping, ORDER BY and LIMIT, so keywords sharing their four text columns still add. Measured 2026-10-17 on the first version of the change (lost with a container restart, query rebuilt from the same source, not re-run on it): answers at 20 M (polled peak 670.4 MiB, 5.6 s) and 24 M (795.8 MiB, 4.6 s), 0 fallbacks, canary ok, ranked values equal to the other shapes; the 28 M built-code cell was lost three times to container recycles (a 45-minute corpus generation does not survive one) and is a 0.5.1 item; the 2026-10-17 standalone run of the same shape answered at 28 M (polled peak 914.7 MiB, 43 MiB spare). Stop near 29 to 30 M mentions is extrapolated: INFERRED. Red without: the plan test (the join feeds the text grouping 9 rows, not 87 on the old query); the equality test over 48 combinations on a corpus with duplicate text tuples passes on both, by design. Read and left alone: the three persisted-store _bulk_insert callers have no wall hold (no behaviour difference since the R172 change).
